I'm trying to get more in a routine of cooking my own meals, but it seems like it always takes ages to prepare everything.

Do any of you Voaters have any tips, tricks, or recipes that I should give a try? I'm specifically trying to limit simple carbs in my diet and force myself to eat more vegetables.
What are some cheep, quick and healthy meal ideas?

Vietnamese spring rolls. The rice paper wraps are cheap, and you can basically fill the roll with whatever you want. Grill some chicken (or shrimp, tofu, or any other protein), shred some carrots and lettuce (other greens), throw in some cilantro or basil, roll it up and you're done. You can pretty much put anything in the roll and make some homemade peanut sauce for a healthy, low carb meal. I ate a fuckton of these when I first graduated from college and was dead broke.

buy frozen rice from your local grocery store (usually takes about 3mins in the microwave to cook up). In a medium sized pan add about 2 tablespoons of soy sauce, and 2 tablespoons of water. Place a chicken thigh in said pan, cook on medium high w/ spices (no salt needed, that came from the soy sauce. I do recommend smoked piperka, onion powder, curry powder, and ground ginger) until thoroughly cooked. Combine chicken and rice. Delicious ~15min meal for less than 10 bucks. If you're feeling fancy, cook up some veggies on the side and impress your SO with your culinary skills.

/v/eatcheapandhealthy hasn't picked up much steam yet, but my advice would be to stay as simple as possible. Here's a quick and simple example (cheapness relative to your local food prices):

Preheat the oven to 425F. Take a raw chicken breast, shake some dry rub spice on it (here my current favourite), flip it over and shake some on the other side. Place the chicken on a pan and bake for 25 minutes. About 10 minutes before the chicken is done, grab a pot and your vegetable steamer. Get the water boiling and put some broccoli in for about 6 minutes. Time it so both finish at about the same time. A bit of salt and pepper on the broccoli, or a little bit of shredded cheddar cheese is just right.

If you (or anyone else) wants to add some carbs, get a small sauce pot (1qt), add some salt-free vegetable bouillon, a little bit of butter, 1/2 cup of water, and 1/4 cup of rice (normal, long cook rice, not minute rice). Bring the water to a boil, stir once, then cover and reduce to a simmer. Start this about 10 minutes before you put the chicken in.

Take any instant noodle, add boiled eggs,ketchup,soy sauce(as your liking) and some boiled/fried veggies to it , simple instant and delicious plus eggs and veggies will increase the quantity, add to the nutrient value without increasing the carb content

Stir-fry. Start heating some oil in a pan with chopped onions and/or garlic. Just chop up vegetables and throw them in the pan with some protein. Add spices, and cook until it tastes good. It's hard to mess up, and you can customize to your liking.

Also chili. Along the same lines, just add a lot more meat/beans/and whatever veggies you want. You can make much bigger batches of this and just freeze/refrigerate the extra, heating up on the stove or microwave later.

Cook some rice. While the water boils prepare your stuff. Get your rice portion ready, Take the veggies and meat out the fridge. Here's what i use, but take any meat and veggies you like. Dont be afraid to take things you like and putting them together. So while the water boils, I start slicing my chicken breast into strips. Chicken drumsicks are cheaper, and those you can just strip with your fingers. Having them in stripes is much faster to cook. When the water is boiling, put the rice in there, a pinch of salt, a little butter/margarine/oil, stir a little. Finish preparing the meat, if you have a wok dump them in there with some oil, but any pan will do. Cook at medium high, toss them around once in a while. Spices is a must, kinda expensive when you buy them, but lasts very long. With chicken I'll use cajun or curry. Chili goes well with beef. So while the meat is cooking, I'll cut the broccoli, mushrooms and onions. Once the chicken starts to get golden, throw the veggies in, add a little oil. A little salt and pepper. Italian seasoning spice is pretty good with veggies, I also love rosemary. Its important to wait until the chicken is almost done, as veggies do not need to be cooked long. The more you cook them, the more you lose nutrients and flavor. 2-3 minutes while mixing it all up in the pan is enough. Follow the instruction for the rice, its usually 10-15 min to cook, then 5 mins off the oven but still with the lid on. Put the veggies and meat with the rice, and voila! I'm used to making it, so my timing is pretty good. I used to slice the meat and cut the veggies before starting the rice, but found out that it was all cooked way before the rice. Peppers are a good fit too. Something I was told revealed to be true: if you like it (veggie, meat or whatever) and its fresh, then its gonna be good. Hope all this is easy to follow and helps you! :P

Another tip maybe, especially at first when everything takes more time. Chop your vegetables and meat while watching a tv show or movie, so you dont feel like youre wasting time.

Stuffed bell peppers! You can throw so many things in there and it always turns out delicious. My favorite stuffing includes:

-Cooked quinoa with a little soy sauce soaked in

-Ground turkey meat seasoned with salt, pepper, Worcestershire sauce, garlic, and paprika

-Sautéed onion, mushroom, and zucchini seasoned with salt and pepper

-Small can of tomato sauce

You mix all that together and then stuff those peppers, throw them in a 350 degree oven for about 25 minutes and BAM, delicious meal. You can also top them with cheese if you're feeling adventurous. I like cheddar and havarti!
